content: Chrome Web Store rejection codes are colour-element names emailed to the publisher. Key ones for a content-script extension: Purple Potassium = excessive/unnecessary permissions ('prevent excessive and unnecessary access to user data'); Blue Argon = MV3 package requirements, most often remotely hosted code or unsafe execution; Red Titanium = obfuscated code or concealed functionality; Purple Lithium = privacy disclosure; Purple Nickel = prominent disclosure before collecting user data; Yellow Zinc = missing/insufficient listing metadata ('Users should be able to understand what features and functionality an item provides based on its listing before they choose to install it'); Yellow Potassium = minimum functionality ('Extensions must provide a basic degree of functionality and utility that provide value to the catalog'); Red* = single purpose. Permissions policy requires 'the narrowest permissions necessary', 'least access' when several options exist, and forbids future-proofing with unused permissions.
